20.0.0.en: God commands that anyone who offers one of his children as a human sacrifice to the god Molech, the god of the children of Ammon, out of fear of him, shall be put to death. This sin was mentioned in (ch. 18:21), but here the punishment is stated, which is death by stoning. This is carried out either by striking him with stones until he dies, or by binding him and throwing him down from a height onto a large stone and placing another large stone on his chest until he dies.

20.1.0.en: God declares His anger against the man who gave one of his children to the pagan god Molech, and decrees that He will destroy him, because by this deed he has defiled the sanctuary of God, which is His house and His people; that is, he has offended and defied God by this great evil.

20.2.0.en: If the clan of this wicked man cooperates with him and hides him, out of fear for him or of him, they thereby help him in his evil, so God declares that He will destroy him and destroy them.

20.2.1.en: Do not cover up sin, for by this you encourage it and make the wicked persist in it. Be strong and proclaim the truth, and care about the salvation of the souls around you; but present the word of God in the manner suited to the one to whom you present it, so that you may draw his heart to the fear of God and he may turn back from his evil.

20.3.0.en: Here God also decrees the punishment of whoever deals with mediums, sorcerers, familiar spirits and all who deal with demons: that he must perish and die. This sin was mentioned in (ch. 19:31).

20.4.0.en: Finally God commands them and warns them about the life of holiness in which they ought to live, because He is holy. If they are His people, they must be holy to Him, that is, they must not worship any god other than Him and must keep away from all pagan practices, and, on the other hand, they must keep His commandments and apply them in their lives.

20.5.s.en: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

20.5.0.en: His blood shall be upon him: he shall be put to death.

20.5.1.en: The fifth commandment, as well as the Law (ch. 19:3), requires the honoring of parents. But whoever does not respect them, and instead dishonors them and insults them with cursing, does not respect God, nor those who are older than himself, foremost among whom are his parents; he has not appreciated their labors in his birth and upbringing. He is ungrateful, and therefore God commands that he be put to death.

20.6.0.en: God declares the punishment for adultery with a married woman, which is death, carried out by stoning (Deut 22:22). But if she is a virgin, he marries her and pays a fine (Deut 22:28, 29). For adultery with a married woman is an assault on the oneness of the marriage and on the belonging of each to the other, whereas in the second case it is possible to marry her as a remedy for the wrong, and he is punished by paying a fine because he assaulted her and did not marry her like the other girls.

20.7.0.en: Whoever dares to commit adultery with his father's wife must be put to death, whether he did this during his father's lifetime or after his death, because his father's wife stands in the place of his mother; he has assaulted motherhood and defied God.

20.8.0.en: Whoever commits adultery with his daughter-in-law must be put to death, because he did not respect his fatherhood toward her, and through his lust he has set himself against God and against all values.

20.9.0.en: Whoever falls into sexual perversion by having a physical relationship with a male has burned with his lust against all the natural laws that God created. He is like an animal in his lust and must be put to death.

20.10.0.en: If a man marries a woman and her daughter at the same time, or marries the mother and then the daughter, or the reverse, that is, the daughter and then the mother, whether during the lifetime of both or after the death of one of them, he has assaulted motherhood by his marriage to the girl's mother, and daughterhood by his marriage to the mother's daughter, and so he must be put to death.

20.11.0.en: Their blood shall be upon them: there is no sin upon whoever kills them, because they deserve it.

20.11.1.en: This base sin, adultery with animals, was spoken of before in (ch. 18:23), and the punishment was the death of the man or woman who committed it, and of the animal, not because the animal had sinned, but to be rid of every trace of evil and uncleanness.

20.11.2.en: If you have sinned by adultery in any form, whether in word or deed, in any manner, do not be content with repentance, confession and Holy Communion alone. Keep away also, as far as you can, from everything associated with the sin, from persons and places, and get rid of any pictures or belongings that remind you of the sin, so that you begin a new, pure page with God.

20.12.0.en: Whoever marries his sister, whether his full sister or his half-sister, is punished by being cut off from the people of God, because he did not preserve the purity of the relationship between brothers and sisters.

20.13.0.en: The fountain of her blood: her reproductive organs from which the blood flows.

20.13.1.en: If a man has a physical relationship with his wife during her monthly period, or during her illness with a disease that causes her to bleed, and does so deliberately and not by oversight (ch. 15:24, 18:19), both of them are punished by being cut off from the people of God, because they indulged in lust even though the woman's health condition did not suit such a union.

20.14.0.en: He also warns against marrying a maternal or paternal aunt, because she is among the relatives whom it is forbidden to marry (ch. 18:12, 13, ch. 18:6). If two dare to enter into this wrong relationship, they bear the guilt of this sin and its punishment, which is being cut off from the people of God.

20.15.0.en: If a man marries his uncle's wife, he has transgressed the law of forbidden marriages, for she stands in the place of his aunt, that is, his mother. They bear the punishment of this sin, which is most likely being cut off from the people of God, in addition to their becoming childless, and this means:

20.15.1.en: 1- God strikes them with barrenness, so that they have no children.

20.15.2.en: 2- Or their children born of them die.

20.15.3.en: 3- Or the children born are considered illegitimate, because God is not pleased with this relationship.

20.16.0.en: The Law had already declared the prohibition of marrying the wife of a brother, whether during his lifetime if he had divorced her, or after his death if she had borne children (ch. 18:16). If this happens, it is considered a crime and an uncleanness, because he has dishonored his brother, that is, he did not respect the feelings of brotherhood, and their punishment is childlessness, as was explained in the previous verse.

20.17.s.en: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

20.17.0.en: God reminds them of the importance of keeping His commandments and worshiping Him so that they may remain in the Promised Land, and of not taking part in the worship of idols like the pagan inhabitants of the land, lest this holy land vomit them out, that is, the land which God sanctified by dwelling in it and by their holy worship. Because God hated the evils of the original inhabitants of the land, He drove them out of it and settled the children of Israel in it in their place, because they were distinguished by the worship of God and by holiness, so they received the good things of the land, which is described as flowing with milk and honey.

20.18.0.en: God reaffirms to them the law of the foods permitted from clean animals and birds, together with keeping away from eating the unclean animals and birds which He distinguished, that is, defined, for them.

20.19.0.en: God demands holiness of them, that is, that they worship Him alone and keep away from all evil, for two reasons:

20.19.1.en: 1- Because He is holy and righteous, and they can live with Him and enjoy fellowship with Him.

20.19.2.en: 2- Because God has distinguished them from the other peoples with many blessings, and therefore they have no need of the pagan gods, who are demons, and of all their evils that corrupt the soul.

20.19.3.en: Remember, when Satan presents any sin to you, that the holy God, your heavenly Father, is looking at you. Do not defile yourself with sin and separate yourself from Him, so that you are deprived of His blessings, His fellowship and His love. Hold fast to holiness, for it is your means of enjoying peace and joy forever.

20.20.0.en: The gravity of the sin of dealing with demons, who are called familiar spirits, and of those who deal with them, who are called sorcerers, was spoken of before (ch. 19:31). If anyone transgresses this commandment and deals with demons, his guilt is great and he is punished by death by stoning.

20.20.1.en: The Book of Exodus: The holiness of the priests

21.0.0.en: The Law forbids the priest to take part in the burial rites of any person, because death is connected with sin and is therefore considered an uncleanness, and whoever touches or takes part in the burial of a dead person becomes unclean. The priest is the example of holiness for all the people.

21.1.0.en: The priest is allowed an exception for seven near relatives, whom he may take part in burying without being defiled, because he is directly responsible for them. These relatives are:

21.1.1.en: The father, the mother, the son, the daughter, the brother, the unmarried sister, and the wife.

21.1.2.en: As for the married sister, her husband is responsible for her. As for the wife, as is made clear in (v. 4), he is not defiled by taking part in her burial, because he and she are one flesh, and she is the one referred to as his kin (v. 4). But as for the rest of the kin and relatives, whatever their rank, he must not defile himself by burying them.

21.2.0.en: He warns them against practices that were offered to the pagan gods, such as:

21.2.1.en: 1- Making a bald spot on the head by shaving all sides of the head and leaving a circle of hair on top of the head.

21.2.2.en: 2- Shaving the hair from the sides of the beard, that is, the two sides, and leaving the middle part on the chin, in order to please the gods.

21.2.3.en: 3- Making cuttings in the various parts of the body.

21.2.4.en: If the whole people are forbidden to do these pagan practices, how much more the priest, who is their highest example, so that his worship is wholly for God and not for idols.

21.3.0.en: Here He declares the importance of the holiness of the priests and of their keeping away from burying the dead or from pagan practices, for the following reasons:

21.3.1.en: 1- Because their lives are set apart, consecrated and holy to God.

21.3.2.en: 2- Because they are the highest example for the people in hallowing the name of the Lord, so that the people may follow their example.

21.3.3.en: 3- Because they offer the offerings and burnt offerings to God in His house, and because of their greatness, the one who offers them needs to be holy.

21.3.4.en: Do not forget that you are holy to God, so give Him your whole heart and not sin and the world. And if you sin, wash your heart by repentance and confession, and sanctify also your thoughts, your words and your deeds, so that you may be an example for others and a light to the world.

21.4.0.en: The priest represents perfection and is an example for the people, so he must also be careful about his marriage:

21.4.1.en: 1- The wife he chooses must not be known among the people for immorality, lest she return to her immorality and cause the people and her husband to stumble.

21.4.2.en: 2- She must not be defiled by any evil deed well known among the people, such as theft, lest she trouble the priest by her conduct and cause the people to stumble.

21.4.3.en: 3- His wife must not have been married before and divorced, lest the reason for her divorce was bad conduct and she return to it.

21.5.0.en: God addresses the people and asks them to regard the priest as holy in their eyes, because he offers the offerings of the Lord, and God sanctified him on the day of his ordination. The effect of the people's hallowing of the priest appears in: The Book of Exodus

21.6.0.en: Here He stresses the importance of the priest's taking care in raising his children, because he is an example for the people, and therefore He makes the punishment severe for the priest's daughter if she falls into immorality. If any virgin commits adultery, she is stoned, but the priest's daughter is burned with fire, as a declaration of God's anger against her, to wipe out the stumbling block she could cause the people, and as a declaration of the priest's rejection of this shameful conduct, because her immorality has defiled the house of the priest and become a disgrace and an object of the people's mockery. Her burning with fire confirms the purity of the priest and puts the fear of God in the hearts of the people.

21.7.s.en: (2) The holiness of the high priest

21.7.0.en: The chief priest: the high priest.

21.7.1.en: In this verse and the following verses God speaks about the high priest, on whose head the oil was poured on the day of his consecration, whose hand was filled, that is, who began to offer the sacrifices, and who put on the splendid garments of the high priest. He is the highest example for the priests and the people, and he is responsible for the care of the priests. So he must not indulge in displays of grief and distress by uncovering his head and tearing his clothes, as some of the people do, because his sorrows have hope, and by his composure he is an example to others.

21.7.2.en: The high priest is a type of Christ, so he does not uncover his head, that is, his dignity, and does not tear his clothes, which signify the Church.

21.8.0.en: God forbids him to take part in the burial rites of any dead person, even if it is his father or mother. He is an example of purity and of keeping away from any uncleanness, although the ordinary priest is permitted to take part in the burial of the seven near relatives (vv. 2-4).

21.9.0.en: The sanctuary: the tabernacle of meeting.

21.9.1.en: Here He confirms that the high priest is not to take part in anyone's funeral or in any trouble that requires him to go out from the tabernacle of meeting, because he serves God in His house, and it is not right for him to go out and leave the service, for it is more important than any other worldly work. He supports this by the fact that upon his head are the crowns of glory and honor which he received through the pouring of the oil on his head, so that he may come forward and stand in the presence of God; therefore it is not right for him to leave God for any reason.

21.10.0.en: It is required in the choice of his wife that she be a virgin, for he is a type of Christ, who betrothed the Church to Himself as a virgin, so that all her feelings and her love are for Him.

21.10.1.en: He does not marry a widow, lest she make a comparison between him and her first husband, which may cause problems. And he does not marry a divorced woman, that is, one who entered into problems with her first husband, so that she may be at peace and suitable for union with this great position of leadership, the position of the high priest.

21.10.2.en: And he does not marry a woman of immorality who has been defiled by this sin, for she does not suit this great position, which needs great purity.

21.10.3.en: This virgin must of course be a Jewess, that is, from his own people, because foreign women were associated with the worship of idols; that is, she ought to be a believer in God and live with Him.

21.11.0.en: One of the reasons for the care in choosing the wife is that the high priest may have blessed offspring, not defiled because of the morals and conduct of their mother, so that he does not expose his position of leadership to the talk of the people, or to being a stumbling block for him. In addition, his sons will be priests, and if an impure and careless mother raises them, they will be wicked. God affirms that He has sanctified him and set him apart for His service, so his whole family must be pure and set apart for Him.

21.11.2.en: Care for the holiness of your home, your wife and your children, by looking after them, showing them love, and binding them to the Church, so that it may be a Christian home that glorifies God, and you may be an example to those around you and enjoy an atmosphere that helps you grow spiritually.

21.12.0.en: Here He mentions the physical conditions that must be met by the priest so that he may be without blemish, for he is a type of Christ, the Lamb without blemish, and so that his permanent defect may not hinder him from the service of God. This applies throughout the service of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levites "in their generations", that is, it is not applied in the New Testament, because these physical defects signify spiritual defects; if the latter, the spiritual ones, are found in the New Testament, he is barred from the priesthood.

21.13.0.en: Here He specifies the physical defects that bar from the priesthood. They are not applied in the New Testament, but if a disability exists that prevents the priest from carrying out his service, in that case he is barred only from the priesthood. The grounds for exclusion in the Old Testament are:

21.13.1.en: 1- A blind man: this signifies the lack of spiritual insight and spiritual understanding.

21.13.2.en: 2- A lame man: this signifies the uprightness lacking in his conduct.

21.13.3.en: 3- One who has a flat nose: that is, one with a deformity of the nose, so that he cannot distinguish well by smell; this signifies weakness in distinguishing between right and wrong.

21.13.4.en: 4- One who has anything superfluous: that is, one who has any excess growth on his body, such as an extra finger; this signifies excessive preoccupation with the world.

21.14.0.en: 5- One who has a broken foot or broken hand: this would hinder him from performing his service, and it appears that the setting of fractures at that time was not completely possible; it signifies weakness in the capacity for spiritual work and sound conduct.

21.15.0.en: 6- Crookbackt: that is, one with a bowed back, and this prevents him from performing the service successfully. It signifies one burdened with the load of many sins on his back who does not feel them.

21.15.1.en: 7- A dwarf: that is, one from whom some part of his body is missing, such as the nose or a finger. The dwarf is counted as one of its kinds, and this hinders him from his service and signifies the person who is lacking in his spiritual relationship with God.

21.15.2.en: 8- One who has a blemish in his eye: this is a white cloud that obscures sight and signifies weakness in spiritual discernment.

21.15.3.en: 9- Scurvy: this is one who has a skin disease that makes him inclined to scratch. It signifies one on whom the marks of sin appear and who causes others to stumble.

21.15.4.en: 10- Scabbed: this is one who has patches differing from the color of the skin on his face and on some parts of his body. It signifies one whose life sin disfigures and who causes others to stumble.

21.15.5.en: 11- Having his stones broken: this is one to whom an accident has happened, or who was struck on his testicles, or who has a disease that weakens them. It signifies spiritual weakness and preoccupation with lusts.

21.16.0.en: In conclusion, God affirms that the priest should have no physical defects, so that they do not hinder him from his service and so that the people may feel that he is perfect, because their outlook in the Old Testament was material. In addition, some of them thought that physical defects were due to sin; this is a mistaken belief, but it existed among them and could confuse their minds concerning the priest and cause him trouble.

21.17.0.en: The most holy and the holy: the foods that the priest takes from the house of the Lord, which are most holy or holy and set apart for him.

21.17.1.en: If a priest of the seed of Aaron has a physical defect among the defects mentioned above and is not permitted to serve in the house of the Lord, he is nevertheless not deprived of his portion of the food and drink that the priest receives, because he does no material work that brings him profit, just as the New Testament teaches that the expenses of the priest's life be provided (1 Cor 9:

21.17.2.en: 11-14), even if he is struck by illness or reaches old age, which hinders him from service.

21.18.0.en: Here He confirms that one who has a defect is not permitted to enter the sanctuary to serve God and to see the veil that separates the sanctuary from the Holy of Holies. Nor may he approach the bronze altar to offer sacrifices, because if he dared and performed a service, he would defile the place by breaking the commandments of God, who sanctified the place and the servants who work in it and barred the one who has a defect from service.

21.19.0.en: Moses taught Aaron and his sons all the preceding commandments concerning the sanctification of the priests mentioned in this chapter, and likewise taught the people all the commandments of God mentioned in the preceding chapters. He is a faithful servant who carries out his work with care.

21.19.1.en: Examine yourself to discover your spiritual defects and your weaknesses of soul, then ask for God's help and the guidance of your father of confession to correct them. And know that God is able to forgive your sins, however many they are, and to complete what is lacking in you, whatever you suffer from.

21.19.2.en: Conditions for the sacrifices offered to God
